title.value: BLIP-3-Video: You Only Need 32 Tokens to Represent a Video Even in VLMs

TLDR.value: We present BLIP-3-Video, which is a compact video-based VLM using 20x less visual tokens compared to the standard models.

abstract.value: We present BLIP-3-Video, a multimodal language model for videos, particularly designed to efficiently capture temporal information over multiple frames. BLIP-3-Video takes advantage of the `temporal encoder' in addition to the conventional visual tokenizer, which maps a sequence of tokens over multiple frames into a compact set of visual tokens. This enables BLIP-3-Video to use much fewer visual tokens than its competing models (e.g., 32 vs. 4608 tokens). We explore different types of temporal encoders, including learnable spatio-temporal pooling as well as sequential models like Token Turing Machines. We experimentally confirm that BLIP-3-Video obtains video question-answering accuracies comparable to much larger state-of-the-art models (e.g., 34B), while being much smaller (i.e., 4B) and more efficient by using fewer visual tokens.

primary_area.value: applications to computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities
